item.title: The High Costs of Defense Budget Uncertainty
item.description: The ubiquity of budgetary “continuing resolutions”—and, increasingly, short-term government shutdowns—has become a disaster for US national security. The post The High Costs of Defense Budget Uncertainty appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Where Are America’s Aircraft Carriers Now?
item.description: Although the US Navy has 11 nuclear-powered aircraft carriers in active service, only around half are deployed at any given time—with the rest in port or undergoing maintenance. The post Where Are America’s Aircraft Carriers Now? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: 2025 Was a Banner Year for UK Military Exports
item.description: The British Ministry of Defence revealed that the UK had sold $27 billion in weapons to foreign customers in 2025—mainly through two large contracts with Norway and Turkey. The post 2025 Was a Banner Year for UK Military Exports appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Kim Jong-un Beware: The US Just Tested Its M270 Rocket Launcher in South Korea
item.description: Though rocket artillery had its origins in the Cold War, the platforms are still highly relevant on the modern battlefield—as seen in Ukraine. The post Kim Jong-un Beware: The US Just Tested Its M270 Rocket Launcher in South Korea appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Supersonic Without the Burn: The Hidden Power of Supercruise
item.description: Supercruise favors high-end air superiority platforms and widens the performance gap between fifth-generation fighters and legacy aircraft. The post Supersonic Without the Burn: The Hidden Power of Supercruise appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why the Flanker Fights Like No Western Jet
item.description: The Flanker platform is famous for airshow maneuvers, but those maneuvers are not merely for entertainment value; they allow the Flanker to win engagements within visual range. The post Why the Flanker Fights Like No Western Jet appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: “Cottonclads” at Dawn: How the Confederacy Snatched Galveston from the Union
item.description: On New Year’s Day 1863, the Confederacy managed to break the Union blockade choking its ports by capturing Galveston, Texas. The post “Cottonclads” at Dawn: How the Confederacy Snatched Galveston from the Union appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Ukraine War in 2025: A Short Review
item.description: Overall, Russia made progress on the battlefield in 2025—yet its advances came at a heavy cost, and there is little evidence of an imminent Ukrainian collapse. The post The Ukraine War in 2025: A Short Review appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: What Zohran Mamdani and New York Can Learn from Afghanistan
item.description: Political elites in New York City, just like American forces in Afghanistan, have become obsessed with the wrong kind of metrics in measuring success. The post What Zohran Mamdani and New York Can Learn from Afghanistan appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why the US Should Recognize South Yemen
item.description: An independent South Yemen could be a force for stability and offer an end to the country’s decade-long civil war. The post Why the US Should Recognize South Yemen appeared first on The National Interest.
